effects: The signer sends the full msg.value in native BTC to the vault (Vault.mint() is payable and the vault keeps all of it).
The signer receives uniBTC (8 decimals) equal to msg.value / 1e10, minted to msg.sender by IMintableContract(uniBTC).mint(_sender, uniBTCAmount) in _mint(address,uint256).
Any part of msg.value below 1e10 wei (under 1 satoshi) is kept by the vault without uniBTC for it and is not refunded.

The call reverts when native BTC is not allowed or is paused, when the service is stopped, when less than 1 satoshi is sent, or when the cap is reached. The signer's assets do not change in those cases.
formats.shown: "Mint uniBTC with <value> BTC", with an always-visible Amount field showing the native value sent, in BTC at 18 decimals.

findings.title: mint(): the amount of uniBTC received is not shown, only the BTC sent; it is value/1e10 at 8 decimals.
findings.evidence: Vault.sol _mint(address,uint256): `(, uint256 uniBTCAmount) = _amounts(_amount); ... IMintableContract(uniBTC).mint(_sender, uniBTCAmount);` and _amounts: `uniBTCAmt = _amount / EXCHANGE_RATE_BASE`. The descriptor's interpolatedIntent "Mint uniBTC with {@.value}" names uniBTC but gives no amount for it. The value is 1:1 in BTC terms, so the BTC amount shown equals the uniBTC received, apart from sub-satoshi dust.
findings.fix: You could say the 1:1 rate in the intent, e.g. "Mint uniBTC 1:1 with {@.value}". No field can show the derived amount.

findings.title: mint(): any value below 1 satoshi (1e10 wei) is kept by the vault and earns no uniBTC.
findings.evidence: Vault.sol _amounts(uint256): `uint256 uniBTCAmt = _amount / EXCHANGE_RATE_BASE;` truncates, and mint() never refunds msg.value minus uniBTCAmt*1e10. The screen shows the full @.value as the Amount, which is what leaves the wallet.
findings.fix: None needed in the descriptor. Wallets that send whole-satoshi amounts avoid the dust.
